model.intended_use: A medical LLM fine-tuned from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for advanced medical reasoning: it generates a complex 'Thinking' trace (reflecting, backtracking, and correcting itself) before producing a 'Final Response' to medical questions.
capabilities: self-reflection and correction of reasoning trajectories (thinks-before-it-answers)
structured '## Thinking' / '## Final Response' output format
limitations: not suitable for real-world clinical or industry applications where inaccuracies could cause harm (per paper's ethical statement)
may still produce hallucinated or inaccurate medical content
trained/evaluated only on English medical benchmarks (this 8B checkpoint)
verifier (GPT-4o) used to build training data is itself imperfect (~94.5-96.5% measured accuracy), so some training signal may be noisy

references.title: HuatuoGPT-o1, Towards Medical Complex Reasoning with LLMs

provenance.notes: HF cardData declares base_model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with a base_model:finetune relation tag. The paper fully discloses the two-stage training method (SFT then PPO-based RL) and the data-construction pipeline, but does not disclose exact code/infra, full compute budget, or the released checkpoint's exact commit-level training log.

methods: supervised fine-tuning on synthesized complex chain-of-thought trajectories
reinforcement learning with PPO using verifier-based sparse rewards
transformation.objective: Adapt the general-purpose instruction-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model into a medical reasoning model that searches for and reflects on complex reasoning paths (Stage 1: SFT) and further improves that reasoning via reward-guided reinforcement learning against a verifiable-answer signal (Stage 2: RL).

stage1_sft.data_size: 20K SFT examples (question, complex CoT, formal response)

stage2_ppo.reward: 1 for verified-correct final answer, 0.1 for incorrect, 0 for missing reasoning structure

transformation.notes: Per the paper, GPT-4o is used both as the generator that synthesizes initial CoT/answers and iteratively applies search strategies (Backtracking, Exploring New Paths, Verification, Correction) to build 'complex CoT' reasoning trajectories, and as the verifier that gives binary True/False feedback comparing a candidate answer against the ground-truth answer (measured verifier accuracy: 96.5% in Stage 1, 94.5% in Stage 2, on 200 manually annotated samples). Three small open models (Gemma2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B) were used earlier in the pipeline purely to filter out multiple-choice questions that were 'too easy' (all three answered correctly), not as generator/verifier for the released training data.

datasets.name: MedQA-USMLE (training set)
datasets.description: USMLE-style multiple-choice medical exam questions; its training split was one of the two source pools of closed-set questions transformed into HuatuoGPT-o1's verifiable medical problems.
datasets.provider: Original MedQA authors (Jin et al.); training set reused by FreedomIntelligence
processing: difficulty filtering (removed questions 3 small LLMs all answered correctly)

datasets.name: MedMCQA (training set)
datasets.description: Indian medical entrance exam multiple-choice questions; its training split was the second source pool of closed-set questions transformed into HuatuoGPT-o1's verifiable medical problems.
datasets.provider: Original MedMCQA authors; training set reused by FreedomIntelligence
processing: difficulty filtering (removed questions 3 small LLMs all answered correctly)

datasets.name: Medical-o1 Verifiable Problem
datasets.description: 40K open-ended medical problems with unique ground-truth answers, converted from a pool of 192K MedQA-USMLE/MedMCQA multiple-choice training questions. 20K used for SFT (stage 1) and 20K reserved for RL (stage 2); paper also mentions 4K unconverted closed-set questions and 5K general (non-medical) verification questions from MMLU-Pro added for domain-compatibility experiments (not part of the released HF dataset).
datasets.size: 40K verifiable medical problems (from a 192K multiple-choice source pool)
processing: difficulty filtering via 3 small LLMs (Gemma2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B)
GPT-4o reformatting from multiple-choice to open-ended question + ground-truth answer

datasets.name: Medical-o1 Reasoning SFT
datasets.description: 20K SFT examples of (question, complex chain-of-thought, formal response) synthesized with GPT-4o by searching for correct reasoning trajectories over the verifiable medical problems, validated via the GPT-4o verifier. Note: the currently distributed HF dataset revision has been split (2025-04-22) to keep only the medical-only SFT file plus a medical+general mix file; the English medical-only file corresponds to the ~20K examples described in the paper.
processing: GPT-4o-guided search for correct CoT trajectories (Backtracking, Exploring New Paths, Verification, Correction)
GPT-4o verifier validation of final answers

safety.risk_level: Paper's own Ethical Statement: the model may still produce hallucinations or inaccuracies and is explicitly not permitted for use in clinical or other industry applications where such inaccuracies could lead to unintended consequences.

items.description: Model may produce hallucinated or medically inaccurate content despite its reasoning/self-correction design.
Not permitted for use in clinical or other industry applications where inaccuracies could lead to unintended consequences; authors state the model 'is not suitable for real-world applications'.
Users are asked to adhere to usage restrictions to safeguard the safety and integrity of downstream applications.

Training data verifier (GPT-4o) reliability was manually audited on 200 sampled scoring instances, showing 96.5% accuracy in Stage 1 and 94.5% in Stage 2, to bound noise introduced by automated verification.
